content:
As previously announced earlier this year, Google Chrome has now switched to releasing updated versions every two weeks.

Previously, Chrome released major "milestone" updates every four weeks, such as upgrading from version 100 to version 101. Before 2021, Google used a six-week update cycle.

The change to releasing major updates every two weeks aims to deliver "new features, performance improvements, and bug fixes" more quickly. While each update contains less content, the update frequency will increase accordingly.

Google also pointed out that this "accelerated update pace is good for the entire web ecosystem." Developers will be able to "roll out modern web features with greater confidence, because the deployment cycle is shorter, interoperability updates can be delivered quickly, and security improvements can also be pushed to users across various platforms more rapidly." Each version has a "smaller scope," which also helps "isolate the source of regression errors more quickly."

In terms of security, Google stated that in the face of new threats brought by artificial intelligence, this change will help "defend against rapidly evolving threats."

As for enterprise customers, Chrome offers an "Extended Stable" channel that updates every eight weeks: first releasing Chrome 156, then version 160. Google indicated that most enterprise users should actually adopt the Stable channel with two-week updates.

Chrome 153 will be rolled out starting today for desktop, Android, and iOS versions. Version 154 will be released on September 22.
